workflows.name: Blocked Indicator Revalidation
workflows.description: Re-checks the oldest standing blocks in Blocked IPs against AbuseIPDB and FortiGuard. IPs at or above the configured AbuseIPDB threshold stay blocked; those that have decayed below it become removal candidates, unless FortiGuard still flags them, in which case they are held back for review. Runs on IPs by default; set enabled_types in the Configuration step to widen it to domains, URLs and hashes, which FortiGuard alone scores. Removal is a dummy step - nothing is deleted.

steps.name: Start
steps.description: Analyst starts the review. The playbook fetches its own batch, so the record selection is not used.

steps.name: Configuration
steps.description: Tuning knobs. abuse_threshold is the AbuseIPDB confidence percentage at or above which an indicator stays blocked. fortiguard_override=yes keeps an indicator FortiGuard still flags even when AbuseIPDB has decayed.

steps.name: Find Blocked IPs
steps.description: Oldest blocked indicators first - those are most likely to have decayed. This fetches a 30-record window; Extract Indicators then filters by enabled type and caps the batch at max_indicators.

steps.name: Extract Indicators
steps.description: Validates each value really is an IPv4 address, drops blanks and duplicates, and trims the batch to max_indicators.

steps.name: Enrich AbuseIPDB
steps.description: One lookup per IP. ignore_errors keeps a single failed lookup from killing the run.

steps.name: Enrich FortiGuard
steps.description: Runs over every enabled indicator type, not just IPs. Second opinion for IPs; the only source for domains, URLs and hashes.

steps.name: Evaluate Against Threshold
steps.description: Buckets every indicator into KEEP or CLEAN against abuse_threshold and records the reasoning for each one.

steps.name: Any Indicators Found
steps.description: Guards the review step so an empty batch still finishes cleanly.

steps.name: Analyst Review
steps.description: Shows the full enrichment table and waits for a decision.
